Equities on the Nigerian Exchange Limited extended their losing streak on Wednesday, with market capitalisation slipping to N158.42tn and the All-Share Index dropping to 243,995.29 points.
The pullback marked a decline from Tuesday’s market capitalisation of N159.52tn and index level of 245,685.87 points, while the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Monetary Policy Rate remained at 23.00 per cent.
Across sector and board indices, pressure was broad-based even as a few pockets posted gains. The NGX Premium Index fell from 31,700.29 to 31,286.51, the NGX 30 declined from 9,044.13 to 8,981.98, and the NGX Banking Index edged down from 2,256.23 to 2,226.80, while the NGX Consumer Goods Index ticked higher from 3,957.00 to 3,960.18 and the NGX Industrial Index rose from 11,599.88 to 11,633.92.
Among individual equities, Fortis Global Insurance led percentage gainers with a 10.00 per cent rise to N1.65, followed by Cornerstone Insurance at 9.92 per cent to N6.65 and Trans-Nationwide Express at 9.91 per cent to N2.33.
On the losing side, Nigerian Aviation Handling Company fell 10.00 per cent to N130.50, McNichols Consolidated dropped 9.57 per cent to N4.25, and AIICO Insurance slid 9.43 per cent to N4.32, alongside a 4.84 per cent drop in MTN Nigeria Communications to N796.50.
In exchange-traded products, NewGold ETF climbed 10.00 per cent to N80,784.00 and Vetiva Banking ETF gained 7.65 per cent to N27.99, while Greenwich Alpha ETF lost 3.85 per cent to N599.98 and Vetiva Industrial ETF dipped 1.86 per cent to N99.10.
Market records showed 29,850 equity trades for a volume of 1,647,067,528 shares, 467 ETP trades for 157,825 units, and 10 bond trades for 555,555 units, with no debt gainers or losers recorded.
